Efficacy of Adjuvant Chemotherapy (5-FU + Levamisole) in Stage II/III Colon Cancer

Phase III Randomized Clinical Trial

Abderrezzaq KADOUCHE

Study Context

This dataset originates from a landmark multi-center, randomized Phase III trial conducted by the NCCTG and the Mayo Clinic (Moertel et al., 1991). It evaluates the efficacy of two post-surgery adjuvant therapies against an observation control group for patients with resected stage II/III colon carcinoma:

* Levamisole: A low-toxicity compound historically used as an animal anti-worm agent.

* 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU): A moderately toxic antimetabolite chemotherapy.

The data features a multivariate failure time structure with two records per patient to track sequential clinical endpoints: recurrence and death.

It also includes a known real-world data inconsistency between the lymph node count (nodes) and its binary threshold (node4).

Aim

The primary objective of this statistical analysis is to determine whether adjuvant chemotherapy combining Levamisole and 5-Fluorouracil significantly prolongs time-to-event outcomes compared to Levamisole alone or simple observation in patients with resected Stage B/C colon cancer.

Variable Labels

The variables are defined and coded as follows:

  • id | Patient identifier (numeric)
  • study | Study code (coded as 1 for all patients)
  • rx | Treatment allocation group:
    • Obs: Observation (Control arm)
    • Lev: Levamisole mono-therapy
    • Lev+5FU: Combined Levamisole and 5-Fluorouracil therapy
  • sex | Patient biological sex (1 = Male, 0 = Female)
  • age | Patient age at study registration (in years)
  • obstruct | Obstruction of the colon by the tumor (1 = Yes, 0 = No)
  • perfor | Perforation of the colon by the tumor (1 = Yes, 0 = No)
  • adhere | Tumor adherence to nearby organs (1 = Yes, 0 = No)
  • nodes | Total number of regional lymph nodes with detectable cancer (integer)
  • time | Follow-up duration: Days until the clinical event occurred or until right-censoring
  • status | Censoring indicator for the specific event type (1 = Event occurred, 0 = Censored / Lost to follow-up)
  • differ | Histological differentiation grade of the tumor:
    • 1: Well differentiated
    • 2: Moderately differentiated
    • 3: Poorly differentiated
  • extent | Extent of local anatomical tumor spread:
    • 1: Submucosa
    • 2: Muscle
    • 3: Serosa
    • 4: Contiguous structures
  • surg | Time elapsed from surgical resection to study registration (0 = Short interval, 1 = Long interval)
  • node4 | Indicator of heavy nodal involvement (1 = More than 4 positive lymph nodes, 0 = 4 or fewer)
  • etype | Clinical event type tracked in the row (1 = Disease recurrence, 2 = Death)
# Si vous analysez la récidive :
data_recurrence <- subset(colon, etype == 1)

# Si vous analysez le décès :
data_death <- subset(colon, etype == 2)

Descriptive Analysis of Continuous Variables

library(prettyR)

vars_quanti <- c("age", "nodes")

describe(
  data_recurrence[, vars_quanti],
  num.desc = c("min", "max", "mean", "median", "sd", "valid.n")
)
## Description of data_recurrence[, vars_quanti]
## 
##  Numeric 
##       min max  mean median    sd valid.n
## age    18  85 59.75     61 11.95     929
## nodes   0  33  3.66      2  3.57     911
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))


# Boucle sur toutes les variables quantitatives avec courbe de densité
for (var in vars_quanti) {
  
  # 1. Tracer l'histogramme en mode "densité de probabilité" (prob = TRUE)
  hist(data_recurrence[[var]],
       main = paste("Distribution of", var), # Titre dynamique
       xlab = var,                           # Nom de la variable sur l'axe X
       ylab = "Density",                     # L'axe Y devient la Densité
       las  = 1,  # Labels horizontaux
       col  = "white",                       # Barres blanches
       border = "black",                     # Contours noirs
       prob = TRUE)                          # OBLIGATOIRE pour la densité
  
  # 2. Calculer et superposer la courbe de densité
  # na.rm = TRUE est crucial car il peut y avoir des NA dans la colonne 'nodes'
  lines(density(data_recurrence[[var]], na.rm = TRUE), 
        col = "red",                         # Courbe en rouge pour le contraste
        lwd = 1)                             # Épaisseur de la ligne

# 3. AJOUT DU CADRE AUTOUR DU GRAPHIQUE
box(col = "black", lwd = 1) 
}

Missing data

Missing data is limited to differ (2.48%) which is the histological differentiation grade of the tumor and nodes (1.94%) which is the total number of regional lymph nodes with detectable cancer.

To address this low missingness rate, a complete-case analysis will be applied.

tab_NA <- data.frame(  
  Variables = names(data_recurrence), 
  n_NA = colSums(is.na(data_recurrence)), 
  percent_NA = round(colMeans(is.na(data_recurrence)) * 100, 2),  
  row.names = NULL )  

print(tab_NA)

Kaplan-Meier Curves

Censoring is assumed to be non-informative.

The Log-Rank test reveals :

  • a significant difference in disease-free survival between the treatment groups (p < 0.0001). We conclude that treatment allocation significantly impacts the time to cancer recurrence.

  • a significant difference in overall survival between the treatment groups (p = 0.0029). We conclude that treatment allocation significantly impacts the time to death.

library(survival)  

library(survminer) 

library(tidyverse)    

# 1. Ajustement du modèle de Kaplan-Meier pour la Récidive par bras de traitement (rx)
fit_recurrence <- survfit(Surv(time = time, event = status) ~ rx, data = data_recurrence)  

# 2. Tracé des courbes de survie sans récidive
ggsurvplot(
  fit_recurrence,    
  data             = data_recurrence,  
  conf.int         = FALSE, # Recommandé à FALSE pour 3 courbes pour éviter les chevauchements visuels
  pval             = TRUE,  
  risk.table       = TRUE,  
  ggtheme          = theme_bw(), # Cadre noir complet et épuré
  legend.title     = "Treatment Arm",  
  xlab             = "Time (days)", 
  ylab             = "Recurrence-Free Probability", 
  legend.labs      = c("Observation", "Levamisole", "Lev + 5-FU"), 
  palette          = c("#E41A1C", "#377EB8", "#4DAF4A"), # Couleurs  bien distinctes
  risk.table.title = "Number at risk",
  title            = "Disease-Free Survival (DFS) by Treatment Arm"
)

# 1. Ajustement du modèle de Kaplan-Meier pour le Décès par bras de traitement (rx)
fit_death <- survfit(Surv(time = time, event = status) ~ rx, data = data_death)  

# 2. Tracé des courbes de survie globale
ggsurvplot(
  fit_death,    
  data             = data_death,  
  conf.int         = FALSE,   
  pval             = TRUE,  
  risk.table       = TRUE,  
  ggtheme          = theme_bw(), 
  legend.title     = "Treatment Arm",  
  xlab             = "Time (days)", 
  ylab             = "Overall Survival Probability", 
  legend.labs      = c("Observation", "Levamisole", "Lev + 5-FU"), 
  palette          = c("#E41A1C", "#377EB8", "#4DAF4A"),  
  risk.table.title = "Number at risk",
  title            = "Overall Survival (OS) by Treatment Arm"
)

Median survival

In the levamisole plus 5-FU group, the median times for both recurrence-free survival and overall survival were not reached. For both endpoints, more than 50% of the patients remained alive and free of disease recurrence at the end of the follow-up period.

surv_median(fit_recurrence)
##       strata median lower upper
## 1     rx=Obs   1236   803  2036
## 2     rx=Lev   1183   797  2067
## 3 rx=Lev+5FU     NA    NA    NA
surv_median(fit_death)
##       strata median lower upper
## 1     rx=Obs   2083  1656  2789
## 2     rx=Lev   2152  1540    NA
## 3 rx=Lev+5FU     NA  2725    NA

Checking the proportional hazards assumption

I.Recurrence

After stratifying the model by histological differentiation grade (differ), heavy nodal involvement (node4), and bowel obstruction (obstruct), the proportional hazards assumption was successfully met. The updated Schoenfeld residual tests yielded a non-significant global test (χ² = 6.97, df = 9, p = 0.64), and no remaining covariates violated the proportionality assumption (all p > 0.05), confirming the validity of the final multivariate model.”

cox_recurrence <-coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ rx +sex+age+obstruct+perfor+adhere+nodes+node4+differ+extent+surg, data = data_recurrence)

cox.zph(cox_recurrence) #test de Schoenfeld 
##             chisq df       p
## rx        0.35805  2 0.83608
## sex       2.04532  1 0.15268
## age       0.00246  1 0.96046
## obstruct  5.36040  1 0.02060
## perfor    0.02471  1 0.87509
## adhere    0.74073  1 0.38943
## nodes     2.47895  1 0.11538
## node4     9.45001  1 0.00211
## differ   12.91735  1 0.00033
## extent    0.20903  1 0.64753
## surg      1.85897  1 0.17274
## GLOBAL   35.50321 12 0.00039
cox_recurrence2 <-coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ rx +sex+age+strata(obstruct)+perfor+adhere+nodes+strata(node4)+strata(differ)+extent+surg, data = data_recurrence)

cox.zph(cox_recurrence2) #test de Schoenfeld 
##         chisq df    p
## rx     0.6234  2 0.73
## sex    1.3914  1 0.24
## age    0.3663  1 0.55
## perfor 0.0911  1 0.76
## adhere 1.8064  1 0.18
## nodes  0.5977  1 0.44
## extent 0.0353  1 0.85
## surg   1.7136  1 0.19
## GLOBAL 6.9695  9 0.64
par(mfrow=c(1,2))

plot(cox.zph(cox_recurrence2))

Conclusion

I.Recurrence

  • The combined levamisole and 5-Fluorouracil regimen was associated with a statistically significant and substantial reduction in the risk of disease recurrence, decreasing the risk by 38% compared to the observation group (HR = 0.62, 95% CI: 0.48–0.78, p < 0.001).

  • In contrast, levamisole mono-therapy did not demonstrate a statistically significant effect on disease recurrence compared to observation (HR = 0.95, 95% CI: 0.76–1.18, p = 0.634).

  • A greater local anatomical tumor spread was a highly significant predictor of recurrence, with each increasing level of invasion multiplying the risk of recurrence by 1.64 (HR = 1.64, 95% CI: 1.29–2.08, p < 0.001).

  • A longer interval from surgical resection to study registration significantly increased the risk of disease recurrence by 31% (HR = 1.31, 95% CI: 1.07–1.61, p = 0.010).

  • A higher number of positive regional lymph nodes was significantly associated with an increased risk of recurrence, showing a 3% risk increase per additional positive node detected (HR = 1.03, 95% CI: 1.00–1.07, p = 0.026).

II.Death

three covariates demonstrated a statistically significant association with all-cause mortality :

  • A longer interval from surgical resection to study registration (surg) was the strongest predictor of death, increasing the risk by 34% (HR = 1.34, 95% CI: 1.08–1.66, p = 0.007).

  • A higher number of positive regional lymph nodes was significantly associated with an increased risk of mortality, with a 4% risk increase per additional positive node detected (HR = 1.04, 95% CI: 1.01–1.07, p = 0.021).

  • Advanced age at study registration was significantly associated with an increased risk of mortality, demonstrating a 1% risk increase per year of age (HR = 1.01, 95% CI: 1.00–1.02, p = 0.025).

  • The combined levamisole and 5-FU regimen showed a trend toward reduced mortality, though it did not achieve formal statistical significance (HR = 0.79, 95% CI: 0.62–1.01, p = 0.055).
